title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 39 — Allotment of securities by company

content.overview: Section 39 regulates allotment of securities offered to the public. It links public allotment to minimum subscription and receipt of the application money, prescribes the application-money floor subject to SEBI regulation, requires refund where the minimum is not achieved within the applicable period, and requires a return of allotment to be filed with the Registrar.
content.glance: Section 39 — Allotment of securities by company
content.study:
Section 39 regulates allotment of securities offered to the public. It links public allotment to minimum subscription and receipt of the application money, prescribes the application-money floor subject to SEBI regulation, requires refund where the minimum is not achieved within the applicable period, and requires a return of allotment to be filed with the Registrar.

Statutory test
1. Public offer: the section applies to securities of a company offered to the public for subscription.
2. Minimum subscription: the amount stated in the prospectus as the minimum amount must have been subscribed before allotment.
3. Application money: the sums payable on application for the stated minimum amount must have been paid to and received by the company through the permitted instrument.
4. Application-money floor: application money for each security is not to be less than five per cent of nominal amount, or such other percentage/amount as SEBI may specify by regulation.
5. Failure to achieve minimum: if the minimum is not subscribed and the application sum is not received within 30 days from issue of the prospectus, or another SEBI-specified period, the amount received must be returned in the prescribed manner and time.
6. Return of allotment: a company having share capital must file a return of allotment with the Registrar in the prescribed manner.
7. Default consequence: non-compliance with the refund or return-of-allotment requirements attracts the statutory continuing/default penalty.

Application
A company receives applications for only 80% of its stated minimum subscription and proposes allotment. Identify section 39(1), test minimum subscription, consider the applicable period under section 39(3), explain the refund obligation, and separately address return-of-allotment filing under section 39(4).

Boundary
Section 39 governs public-offer allotment safeguards; section 42 governs private placement. Section 40 separately addresses recognised-stock-exchange permission and handling of public application monies.

sections.heading: Definition and legislative purpose
sections.body: Section 39 regulates allotment of securities offered to the public, linking allotment to minimum subscription and application money, with refund and return-of-allotment duties.

sections.heading: Operative ingredients
sections.body:
1. Public offer.
2. Minimum subscription before allotment.
3. Application money received.
4. Application-money floor (5% or SEBI-specified).
5. Refund if minimum not achieved in time.
6. Return of allotment filing.
7. Statutory default consequence.

provisions.title: Companies Act s. 39 — Allotment of securities by company

examples.title: Illustration 1
examples.body: A public issue states a minimum subscription of ₹10 crore. Allotment cannot proceed merely because applications were received; the statutory minimum and required application money must first be satisfied.

examples.title: Illustration 2
examples.body: The stated minimum is not reached within the applicable period. The company must return application money in the prescribed manner.

examples.title: Illustration 3
examples.body: Allotment occurs but the prescribed return of allotment is not filed. The filing default attracts the statutory penalty.

hypotheticals.question: A company receives applications for only 80% of its stated minimum subscription and proposes allotment. Advise under section 39.
hypotheticals.analysis: Test section 39(1) minimum subscription, the period under section 39(3), refund, and section 39(4) return of allotment separately.

distinctions.title: Section 39 and section 42 / section 40
distinctions.right: Section 42 private placement; section 40 exchange permission and money ring-fence

rows.right: Different statutory trigger; do not merge regimes

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 39 as a rule for every private placement.
misconceptions.correction: Private placement is governed by section 42.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring SEBI power to vary the application-money floor.
misconceptions.correction: Section 39 allows SEBI to specify another percentage or amount by regulation.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should section 39 be analysed on public-allotment facts?
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
I. ISSUE: Whether section 39 bars or conditions the proposed allotment.
II. RULE: Minimum subscription, application money, floor, refund period, return of allotment.
III. APPLICATION: Map each ingredient to the facts.
IV. CONCLUSION: State only the consequence supported by the current text.
